rule.name: Azure VM with Password Authentication Enabled
rule.rule_desc: The checked code implements an identity, access-control, or abuse-prevention decision. Determine the trusted verifier, protected resources, and whether the control is enforced on every relevant path.
rule.vuln_desc: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness.
rule.developer: Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.
rule.reviewer: Confirm all Linux VMs use SSH key authentication exclusively. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Azure Storage Account Allows Public Blob Access
rule.rule_desc: Storage configuration may permit public object access. Resolve bucket or container policies, object ACLs, and provider-level public-access controls.
rule.vuln_desc: Unauthenticated users may read private objects or modify publicly writable content if effective access rules grant those operations. A permissive account-level option alone does not establish that every object is public.
rule.developer: Disable unnecessary public access, enforce narrow identity-based permissions, and verify effective object access from an unauthenticated client. Separate intentionally public content from private storage.
rule.reviewer: Confirm no storage accounts allow public blob access unless explicitly serving public-facing content. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Azure Storage Account Without Secure Transfer Required
rule.rule_desc: Storage configuration does not require authenticated encrypted transport for client access.
rule.vuln_desc: A network attacker may intercept storage data or URL-carried access tokens if clients use permitted cleartext requests.
rule.developer: Require secure transfer and verify HTTPS on all storage clients, redirects, and shared-access URLs. Remove cleartext exceptions for private data.
rule.reviewer: Confirm all storage accounts enforce HTTPS. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Azure NSG Rule Allows All Inbound Traffic
rule.rule_desc: The code uses a low-level memory, formatting, allocation, or type-conversion operation whose safety depends on bounds, types, initialization, and caller invariants.
rule.vuln_desc: A violated memory or formatting invariant may expose process memory, corrupt application state, crash the process, or permit code execution when an attacker can influence the relevant inputs.
rule.developer: Validate sizes and types before use, use bounded and type-safe APIs, and keep format strings fixed. Prefer checked conversions and safe ownership abstractions; document and test every remaining unsafe invariant.
rule.reviewer: Confirm open inbound rules are intentional and that resources have application-layer controls. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

rule.name: Azure SQL Server Allows All Azure Services
rule.rule_desc: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
rule.vuln_desc: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
rule.developer: Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.
rule.reviewer: Confirm the 0.0.0.0/0.0.0.0 firewall rule is not used for production SQL servers. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
